learn.title: Short links and link-in-bio, explained for beginners
learn.lead: Common questions about URL shortening, what kurl does, and how a profile page differs from a single short link.

q1.a:
URL shortening replaces a long address (e.g. https://example.com/very/long/path?utm_source=...) with a short one (e.g. kurl.me/abc1234). Short link and shortened URL mean the same thing.

It's useful where character limits matter (social posts) and where people type the URL by hand (business cards, posters). Shorteners also count clicks, so you can see which channels bring people in.

q2.q: How is a short link different from a link-in-bio page?
q2.a:
A short link is a 1:1 mapping: one long URL → one short URL. Best for a single destination, like a Twitter post, an Instagram comment or a business card.

A link-in-bio page collects many links behind one URL. Since Instagram lets you put only one link in your profile, creators use yourname.kurl.me as that one link, pointing visitors to a mini page with their email, booking, store, blog, and socials.

kurl does both: it shortens individual URLs and builds a profile page that bundles them.

q3.a:
kurl is a free URL shortener and link-in-bio service. There are no ads, and you can shorten links without signing in.

Sign in to see stats by device, country and channel. Your links stay until you delete them, and you can build a profile page at an address like yourname.kurl.me.

q4.q: What can a profile page contain?
q4.a:
Mix blocks such as a photo, bio, contacts (phone/email/address), socials, events, galleries, product cards and booking links.

A cafe owner might show a map, opening hours, Instagram and reservation links, and a menu gallery. An instructor: workshop events, a 1:1 booking link and a portfolio. A DJ: upcoming gigs, a Spotify Artist link and photos. All on one page.

q5.q: How deep do the analytics go?
q5.a:
For each short link: total clicks, human vs bot, unique visitors, daily and hourly charts, a day-of-week × hour heatmap, country and city, device, browser, OS, referrer hosts and UTM campaigns. All of it is free.

Profile pages have their own visit stats with the same breakdowns.

q6.a:
Every feature is free: shortening, analytics, profile pages, every block type and custom domains.

There's no paid plan, and no ads.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: kurl collects only the minimum personal data needed to run the Service and anonymizes by default. This policy follows Korea's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and the EU GDPR (Article 13).

sections.p: Sign-in: email (including Apple's private email relay if you use Apple), auth provider (Google or Apple), signup date. Shortening: original URL, short code, expiry. Content: your posts, comments, profile, and uploaded images (EXIF metadata such as capture location is stripped on upload). If you enable push notifications: an APNs device token (iOS app) or web push subscription. On shortened-link clicks, post views, and public profile visits: timestamp, User-Agent, Referer, traffic source (UTM, etc.), IP with the last octet masked, GeoIP-derived country/region/city, browser language, device type/OS/browser, and network operator (ASN/organization). For repeat-visit stats we derive and store a one-way hash (a pseudonymous identifier) from IP and User-Agent; the raw IP itself is not stored. For operation and security we keep request logs (timestamp, path, status code, latency, and when signed in, a user identifier and short code) for a limited period. If a visitor submits a profile's email capture form: the email they enter and an IP hash. On post pages we also collect reading-behavior events to improve the Service: scroll depth reached, visible reading time, and the kind of element clicked within the post screen. These events are linked only by a temporary session ID that disappears when the tab closes and by the pseudonymous hash above; no tracking cookies are used, and no pseudonymous hash is created when your browser sends a GPC (Global Privacy Control) signal. When you read or save content: reading history and bookmarks (reading list, stored with your account only while signed in). Both are visible only to you and can be deleted at any time.

We process data to run the Service (redirects, stats, content publishing), for product analytics to improve the Service, to prevent abuse, and to respond to security incidents. Our legal bases are performance of the user agreement (redirects, content), legitimate interests (analytics, abuse, security), and consent (e.g., push notifications). If we introduce advertising in the future, we will give separate notice in advance and obtain any required consent. We do not sell your personal data.

Anonymous links auto-expire after 24h. Authenticated users' links and content persist until you delete them. Expired links and their click events are auto-cleaned 30 days after expiry. When you delete your account, it and its data are hidden immediately and permanently erased after a 30-day grace period; signing in again within that period restores the account. Security/audit logs are kept about 180 days and operational request logs about 90 days before cleanup, and deleting your account anonymizes your identifier left in those logs. Destruction procedure and method: personal data held in electronic files is permanently deleted in a way that makes recovery or reconstruction impossible — this includes the permanent, unrecoverable deletion carried out after the 30-day grace period when you delete your account. Information retained separately under applicable law is destroyed without delay once its retention period ends. Raw reading-behavior events from post pages are automatically deleted after 90 days.
Stored IPs are masked (IPv4 last octet / IPv6 beyond the first two groups). Raw IPs exist only transiently in memory and logs and are never written to the database.

We use these processors to run the Service: Google and Apple (social sign-in), Google Safe Browsing (the shortened destination URL is sent for malware checks), MaxMind GeoLite2 (offline GeoIP — no visitor data leaves our servers), PostHog (product usage analytics), Sentry (error tracking), Cloudflare (CDN and bot filtering), and Amazon Web Services and Vercel (server and frontend hosting). If you enable push notifications, they are delivered via Apple (APNs) and, for web push, the push service chosen by your browser (e.g., Google, Mozilla, Microsoft). An email a visitor submits through a profile's email capture form is shared with that profile's owner. In addition, events for a user's links and blog interactions may be sent to webhooks the user configures (Discord, Slack, or any HTTPS endpoint); the destination and its handling and security are the user's responsibility. If we introduce advertising, we will add the relevant processors to this policy and give advance notice.

Some processors above (Google, Google Safe Browsing, Apple, PostHog, Sentry, Cloudflare, Vercel, Amazon Web Services, and push delivery services) may process data outside Korea, mainly in the United States. (MaxMind GeoLite2 looks up locally and does not send visitor data abroad.) Only the data listed under "What we collect" is transferred, solely for the operations described here, and kept under the same retention rules. Transfers to the US and elsewhere rely on each processor's data processing agreement, including GDPR Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification. Transfer is by network transmission; for questions or to object, contact haroya01@naver.com (objecting may limit some features).

We use essential and functional cookies and local storage: the authentication token that keeps you signed in (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), a temporary cookie for returning from OAuth sign-in, your language and theme, some view preferences, and whether the cookie notice was dismissed. Product analytics (PostHog) uses browser local storage rather than cookies. We currently use no advertising cookies; if we introduce advertising we will give notice and seek consent in advance. The iOS app stores its tokens in the device Keychain instead of cookies. How to refuse cookies: you can refuse cookie storage or delete already-stored cookies in your web browser settings — for example, under [Settings] → [Privacy and security] → [Cookies and site data]. Note, however, that if you refuse cookies essential to operating the service (such as those that keep you signed in), some features may be limited.

You may access, correct, delete, restrict processing of, and withdraw consent for your personal data, and exercise GDPR rights of access (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction (Art. 18), portability (Art. 20), and objection (Art. 21). In particular, you may object at any time to processing based on legitimate interests (such as analytics), and when your browser sends a Global Privacy Control (Sec-GPC) signal we do not generate the repeat-visit hash. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing carried out beforehand. The settings page lets you download your data as JSON or permanently delete your account — the JSON covers your account, links, and click stats; other data such as posts and profile is provided on request at haroya01@naver.com. A visitor who submitted their email through a profile's email capture form may request access, deletion, or opt-out at the same address.
kurl is not directed to children under 14 and does not collect personal data from children under 14 without a legal guardian's consent (16, or the age set by your country's law, for EU residents).
We apply transport encryption (TLS), hashed/encrypted storage of authentication tokens and two-factor secrets, access controls, IP masking, and data minimization.
